title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Originals Counted in a Full-Set Surrender
content:
When the full set of a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` record is surrendered at origin for a telex release, the surrender carries a count of originals. That count is a reconciliation of the document's documentation history, never a figure offered by the caller.

## What exists to be surrendered

An original can be surrendered only if it is in circulation, and an original is in circulation only because the documentation history records it as having been put into circulation and does not record it as having come back or been voided since.

## The count

The count equals the originals put into circulation according to the documentation history, reduced by those the history shows as surrendered and by those it shows as declared void. All entries of the document are included, whatever set they belong to. A result below zero is taken as zero. Because earlier sets are always wholly returned or voided before a later one goes out, what remains equals the originals of the current set that are still circulating; it is always a whole number.

## Worked examples (hypothetical histories)

| Documentation history of the document | Count |
|---|---|
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation | 3 |
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation; 1 declared void | 2 |
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation and 3 declared void; set 2: 3 put into circulation | 3 |

In the last line, six originals were put into circulation and three were declared void, so six reduced by three gives three, all of them belonging to set 2.

## Points of judgement

**The shipper says it is bringing in two originals, while the history shows three circulating. Which figure is entered?** Three, the figure the history yields.
